title: Something went wrong
author: Lareina86
summary: PowerToys 0.100.2 reports a WPF NullReferenceException during a theme-resource change, but the issue has no bug-report ZIP, expected/actual behavior, or current-release confirmation.

status.label: Needs current reproduction data
status.detail: The stack identifies a WPF binding failure, but does not establish a PowerToys-owned root cause or a current-release regression.

next_action.label: Request bug report and current-version retest
next_action.reason: The automated triage and the issue body both identify missing diagnostics and an obsolete 0.100.2 baseline.

fix_assessment.rationale: No linked fix is established. A concrete code fix cannot be supported until a current reproduction and the PowerToys diagnostic ZIP identify the affected binding, view, or theme resource.

proposed_fixes.title: Capture a current diagnostic and isolate the theme-change binding
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Unproven: WPF throws in BindingExpression.SetupDefaultValueConverter while a template is invalidated during a system theme-resource change; the stack alone does not identify which PowerToys binding supplies the invalid value.
plan: Update from 0.100.2 to the current stable release and confirm whether the crash still reproduces.
Immediately after reproducing, attach the PowerToys bug-report ZIP and record the exact theme-change trigger, affected PowerToys window, and whether the crash occurs once or repeatedly.

Use the diagnostic evidence to locate the PowerToys WPF view/style binding that is re-evaluated during the theme change; only then add a narrowly scoped null-safe binding/resource fix and regression coverage.
verification: Retest the same theme-change sequence on the current stable release.
Confirm the diagnostic ZIP identifies the affected PowerToys component and binding path.
After an implementation, repeat the theme change with both light and dark themes and verify no binding exception is raised.

confidence.rationale: The framework stack and theme-change trigger are observed, but the missing diagnostic ZIP, old version, and absent expected behavior leave the PowerToys root cause unconfirmed.

judgment.rationale: The report contains a real-looking WPF NullReferenceException, but it targets 0.100.2 and does not identify the affected PowerToys surface. The current evidence supports requesting a current retest and diagnostics, not asserting a code fix or duplicate.
evidence: Observed: the issue targets PowerToys 0.100.2 from the Microsoft Store.
Observed: the stack fails in WPF BindingExpression.SetupDefaultValueConverter while theme resources are changing.
Observed: no expected behavior, actual behavior, or PowerToys bug-report ZIP is supplied.
Observed: automated triage cites closed issues 42256, 44991, 45219, 46873, and 47244 as possible duplicates, but no linked fix is established on this issue.
Inferred: the failing binding may be in a PowerToys WPF view or style, but the stack does not identify it.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask the author to update to the current stable release, reproduce the theme change, and attach the resulting PowerToys bug-report ZIP before code-level triage.

comment.body: Thanks for the stack trace. This report is against PowerToys 0.100.2, and the WPF stack does not identify which PowerToys binding is failing. Please update to the current stable release, repeat the same theme-change sequence, and confirm whether it still reproduces. If it does, generate and attach a PowerToys bug report immediately afterward, and include the exact theme change and PowerToys window that was open. That information is needed to distinguish a fixed old-version issue from a current PowerToys binding defect.
